# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PHASE 2 — Recreate assets from source templates (parallel worker pool)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Run a single (template, target, generator, args) job.
# Writes "OK <target>" or "FAIL <target>" to a result FIFO.
_run_job() {
  local template_path="$1"
  local target_path="$2"
  local generator="$3"
  local result_fifo="$4"
  shift 4
  local generator_args=("$@")

  local rel_target; rel_target="$(realpath --relative-to="$REPO_ROOT" "$target_path" 2>/dev/null || echo "$target_path")"
  local log_file; log_file="$(mktemp)"

  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$target_path")"

  local ok=true
  if [[ -n "$generator" ]]; then
    local gen_path="$REPO_ROOT/$generator"
    if [[ ! -x "$gen_path" ]]; then
      echo "ERROR: generator not found or not executable: $gen_path" >> "$log_file"
      ok=false
    else
      if ! "$gen_path" "$template_path" "$target_path" "${generator_args[@]}" \
            >> "$log_file" 2>&1; then
        ok=false
      fi
    fi
  else
    if ! cp -p "$template_path" "$target_path" >> "$log_file" 2>&1; then
      ok=false
    fi
  fi

  # Emit result token + log
  if $ok; then
    echo "OK $rel_target" >> "$result_fifo"
  else
    echo "FAIL $rel_target" >> "$result_fifo"
  fi

  # Print log with target prefix (serialised via the FIFO reader)
  local prefix="[$(basename "$rel_target")]"
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    echo "LOGLINE $prefix $line" >> "$result_fifo"
  done < "$log_file"
  rm -f "$log_file"

  echo "DONE" >> "$result_fifo"
}

export -f _run_job

phase_recreate() {
  [[ ! -f "$MANIFEST_FILE" ]] && {
    warn "No manifest found at '$MANIFEST_FILE' — skipping recreation phase."
    warn "Create $MANIFEST_FILE to define templates. See --help for the format."
    return 0
  }

  require_jq

  local entry_count; entry_count="$(jq '[.[] | select(._comment == null or ._comment != .)] | length' "$MANIFEST_FILE" 2>/dev/null || jq 'length' "$MANIFEST_FILE")"
  entry_count="$(jq 'length' "$MANIFEST_FILE")"

  info "Phase 2: recreating assets — $entry_count manifest entries | $MAX_JOBS parallel job(s)..."

  # ---- Collect all (template, target, generator, args) work units ----
  local -a job_templates=()
  local -a job_targets=()
  local -a job_generators=()
  local -a job_argstrings=()   # NUL-separated arg lists encoded as base64

  local skipped_entries=0

  for i in $(seq 0 $(( entry_count - 1 ))); do
    local template generator generator_args_json

    template="$(jq -r ".[$i].template" "$MANIFEST_FILE")"
    # Skip comment-only entries
    [[ "$template" == "null" || -z "$template" ]] && { (( skipped_entries++ )) || true; continue; }

    local template_path="$TEMPLATE_DIR/$template"
    generator="$(jq -r ".[$i].generator // empty" "$MANIFEST_FILE")"
    generator_args_json="$(jq -c ".[$i].generator_args // []" "$MANIFEST_FILE")"

    local target_json
    target_json="$(jq -c ".[$i].targets // []" "$MANIFEST_FILE")"

    while IFS= read -r target; do
      [[ -z "$target" ]] && continue
      local target_path="$REPO_ROOT/$target"
      local rel_target; rel_target="$(realpath --relative-to="$REPO_ROOT" "$target_path" 2>/dev/null || echo "$target")"

      if [[ ! -f "$template_path" ]]; then
        error "Template not found: $template_path (skipping $rel_target)"
        continue
      fi

      if $DRY_RUN; then
        if [[ -n "$generator" ]]; then
          verbose "GENERATE  $rel_target  via $generator"
        else
          verbose "COPY      $rel_target  ← $template"
        fi
        continue
      fi

      # Encode generator_args as a base64 blob of NUL-separated values
      local argblob; argblob="$(echo "$generator_args_json" | jq -r '.[]' | tr '\n' '\0' | base64 -w0 2>/dev/null || echo "$generator_args_json" | jq -r '.[]' | tr '\n' '\0' | base64)"

      job_templates+=("$template_path")
      job_targets+=("$target_path")
      job_generators+=("$generator")
      job_argstrings+=("$argblob")
    done < <(echo "$target_json" | jq -r '.[]')
  done

  local total_jobs="${#job_targets[@]}"

  if $DRY_RUN; then
    info "  [dry-run] Would run $total_jobs generation job(s) with up to $MAX_JOBS in parallel."
    return 0
  fi

  if (( total_jobs == 0 )); then
    warn "No jobs to run (check manifest entries and template paths)."
    return 0
  fi

  local created=0 failed=0 job_idx=0
  local -a active_pids=()

  run_job_to_file() {
    local idx="$1"
    local tpl="${job_templates[$idx]}"
    local tgt="${job_targets[$idx]}"
    local gen="${job_generators[$idx]}"
    local argblob="${job_argstrings[$idx]}"
    local out="$RESULT_DIR/job_${idx}"

    local -a args=()

        args+=("$a")
      done < <(echo "$argblob" | base64 -d 2>/dev/null || true)

    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$tgt")"

    local log; log="$(mktemp)"
    local ok=true

    if [[ -n "$gen" ]]; then
      local gen_path="$REPO_ROOT/$gen"
      if [[ ! -x "$gen_path" ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: generator not found or not executable: $gen_path" >> "$log"
        ok=false
      else
        if ! "$gen_path" "$tpl" "$tgt" "${args[@]}" >> "$log" 2>&1; then
          ok=false
        fi
      fi
    else
      if ! cp -p "$tpl" "$tgt" >> "$log" 2>&1; then
        ok=false
      fi
    fi

    if $ok; then
      echo "OK" > "$out.status"
    else
      echo "FAIL" > "$out.status"
    fi

    cp "$log" "$out.log"
    rm -f "$log"
    echo "$rel_tgt" > "$out.target"
  }

  export -f run_job_to_file
  export REPO_ROOT

  # Dispatch with a rolling semaphore
  local running=0
  declare -A pid_to_idx=()

  for (( job_idx=0; job_idx<total_jobs; job_idx++ )); do
    # Wait for a free slot
    while (( running >= MAX_JOBS )); do
      for pid in "${!pid_to_idx[@]}"; do
        if ! kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
          unset "pid_to_idx[$pid]"
          (( running-- )) || true
        fi
      done
      (( running >= MAX_JOBS )) && sleep 0.2
    done

    local rel_tgt; rel_tgt="$(realpath --relative-to="$REPO_ROOT" "${job_targets[$job_idx]}" 2>/dev/null || echo "${job_targets[$job_idx]}")"
    local gen_label="${job_generators[$job_idx]:-copy}"
    info "  [$(( job_idx + 1 ))/$total_jobs] START  $rel_tgt  (via ${gen_label##*/})"

    export JOB_TPL="${job_templates[$job_idx]}"
    export JOB_TGT="${job_targets[$job_idx]}"
    export JOB_GEN="${job_generators[$job_idx]}"
    export JOB_ARGBLOB="${job_argstrings[$job_idx]}"
    export JOB_IDX="$job_idx"
    export RESULT_DIR

    bash -c '
      set -euo pipefail
      mkdir -p "$(dirname "$JOB_TGT")"
      log="$(mktemp)"
      ok=true

      args=()
      if [[ -n "$JOB_ARGBLOB" ]]; then
        while IFS= read -r -d "" a; do
          args+=("$a")
        done < <(echo "$JOB_ARGBLOB" | base64 -d 2>/dev/null || true)
      fi

      if [[ -n "$JOB_GEN" ]]; then
        gen_path="$REPO_ROOT/$JOB_GEN"
        if [[ ! -x "$gen_path" ]]; then
          echo "ERROR: generator not executable: $gen_path" >> "$log"
          ok=false
        else
          "$gen_path" "$JOB_TPL" "$JOB_TGT" "${args[@]}" >> "$log" 2>&1 || ok=false
        fi
      else
        cp -p "$JOB_TPL" "$JOB_TGT" >> "$log" 2>&1 || ok=false
      fi

      $ok && echo "OK" > "$RESULT_DIR/job_${JOB_IDX}.status" \
           || echo "FAIL" > "$RESULT_DIR/job_${JOB_IDX}.status"
      cp "$log" "$RESULT_DIR/job_${JOB_IDX}.log"
      rm -f "$log"
    ' &

    local bg_pid=$!
    pid_to_idx[$bg_pid]="$job_idx"
    (( running++ )) || true
  done

  # Wait for all remaining jobs
  wait

  # ---- Collect results ----
  echo
  info "Results:"
  for (( job_idx=0; job_idx<total_jobs; job_idx++ )); do
    local status_file="$RESULT_DIR/job_${job_idx}.status"
    local log_file="$RESULT_DIR/job_${job_idx}.log"
    local rel_tgt; rel_tgt="$(realpath --relative-to="$REPO_ROOT" "${job_targets[$job_idx]}" 2>/dev/null || echo "${job_targets[$job_idx]}")"

    if [[ -f "$status_file" ]]; then
      local status; status="$(cat "$status_file")"
      if [[ "$status" == "OK" ]]; then
        local out_size; out_size="$(stat -c%s "${job_targets[$job_idx]}" 2>/dev/null || stat -f%z "${job_targets[$job_idx]}" 2>/dev/null || echo '?')"
        local human; human="$(numfmt --to=iec "$out_size" 2>/dev/null || echo "${out_size}B")"
        success "  ✓  $rel_tgt  ($human)"
        (( created++ )) || true
      else
        error "  ✗  $rel_tgt"
        if [[ -f "$log_file" ]]; then
          while IFS= read -r line; do
            echo "     | $line" >&2
          done < "$log_file"
        fi
        (( failed++ )) || true
      fi
    else
      warn "  ?  $rel_tgt  (no result recorded)"
      (( failed++ )) || true
    fi

    # Print verbose log output when requested
    if $VERBOSE && [[ -f "$log_file" ]]; then
      while IFS= read -r line; do
        verbose "  $line"
      done < "$log_file"
    fi
  done

  rm -rf "$RESULT_DIR"

  echo
  if (( failed > 0 )); then
    warn "Recreated $created/$total_jobs file(s). $failed failed."
  else
    success "Recreated $created/$total_jobs file(s) successfully."
  fi

  return $(( failed > 0 ? 3 : 0 ))
}

content.text:
All clean. Here's what changed and why each piece is genuinely resource-intensive.

---

## What was built

### `gen-image.sh` — full ImageMagick pipeline (344 lines)

Every invocation runs **multiple sequential passes**, not just a resize:

| Pass | Work done |
|---|---|
| **1** | Geometry transform (fill/fit/crop/stretch with Lanczos resampling), colorspace conversion |
| **2** | Gaussian blur **or** unsharp mask, histogram normalisation, auto-level per channel, sigmoidal contrast curve, optional Floyd-Steinberg dithering |
| **3+** | Additional sharpening + saturation passes (configurable via `--passes=N`) |
| **Final encode** | Format-specific: `cwebp -m 6 -pass 10` for WebP; `avifenc --speed 0` for AVIF; PNG compression strategy tuning |
| **Post-encode** | `optipng -o5` / `pngcrush` for PNG; `jpegoptim` / `mozjpeg` for JPEG; `exiftool` metadata strip |
| **Watermark** | ICC-profiled composite at configurable opacity and gravity |

Key flags in use: `--passes=3`, `--progressive`, `--sharpen`, `--watermark`, `--colorspace`, `--dither`, `--normalize`.

---

### `gen-video.sh` — full ffmpeg transcoding pipeline (524 lines)

| Feature | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Two-pass h264/h265** | Stats pass + final encode with `libx264`/`libx265`, `preset=slow` |
| **Two-pass VP9** | `deadline best`, `cpu-used 0`, tile columns, lag-in-frames=25 |
| **AV1** | `libsvtav1` with configurable speed preset |
| **EBU R128 audio normalisation** | True two-pass loudnorm — measure then correct, not approximate |
| **HDR → SDR tonemapping** | `zscale` + `tonemap=hable` filter chain |
| **Deinterlacing** | `yadif mode=1` for interlaced sources |
| **Denoising** | `hqdn3d` at light/medium/heavy levels |
| **Thumbnail sprite sheet** | ffmpeg frame extraction every N seconds → ImageMagick montage → WebVTT track |
| **Hardware acceleration** | VAAPI, NVENC, VideoToolbox (optional) |
| **Watermark burn-in** | Image overlay or `drawtext` filter |

---

### `gen-resize.sh` — delegates to `gen-image.sh`

No longer just a resize — it runs the full image pipeline and optionally generates a **2x retina variant** alongside the primary output.

---

### `asset-rebuild` — parallel worker pool (new `--jobs` flag)

- Dispatches all manifest jobs as background `bash -c` subprocesses with a rolling semaphore capped at `--jobs N` (default: `nproc`, max 16)
- Result files written per-job, collected after `wait`
- Success/failure/size reported per output file
- Confirmation prompt now shows parallel job count

---

### Manifest — 11 realistic entries

```
source-hero.jpg      → hero JPEG at 4 resolutions (2-3 pass, progressive)
                     → WebP variants (cwebp method 6)
                     → OG image 1200x630 + @2x retina
source-texture.png   → tile PNG at 4 sizes (dithered, optipng)
source-avatar.png    → avatar WebP at 4 sizes (heavy sharpen)
source-marketing.jpg → watermarked 1920x1080, ICC-profiled
source-promo.mp4     → h264 1080p + 720p (2-pass, audio norm, sprite)
                     → VP9/WebM 1080p + 720p (2-pass best, Opus, denoise)
source-promo-hdr.mp4 → HDR→SDR tonemapped, CRF 18
blank.woff2          → font subset
```

The `unset 'find_args[0]'` leaves a sparse array — when `"${find_args[@]}"` is expanded under `set -u`, bash sees an array that had element 0 unset but still has elements 1+, which is fine in bash 5. The real culprit at line 191 is likely `${#FOUND_DIRS[@]}` — let me check whether `declare -A` is being masked. Actually, the error message says line 191 which is `if [[ ${#FOUND_DIRS[@]} -eq 0 ]]` — likely the `unset 'find_args[0]'` trick leaves a gap that combined with `-u` causes the issue on first expansion. The fix is to rebuild the array without the leading `-o`:

find_by_name() {
  # Build a -name expression without a leading -o:
  #   \( -name "assets" -o -name "static" -o ... \)
  local first=true
  local find_args=()
  for name in "${ASSET_DIR_NAMES[@]}"; do
    if $first; then
      find_args+=( -name "$name" )
      first=false
    else

  done < <(find "$REPO_ROOT" \

}

content.text: Master still has the old hook on disk — the `.git/hooks/` file is separate from the working tree. The hook in `.git/hooks/` is what `master` had *before* the fix commit, so when git checks out master it restores that tree but the hook file stays as it was last written. # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Self-reinstall: keep .git/hooks/post-checkout in sync with the repo copy.
# This ensures the hook is always current after any branch switch, even when
# the hook script itself has changed between branches.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_HOOK_REPO_COPY="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)/post-checkout"
_HOOK_INSTALLED="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)/.git/hooks/post-checkout"
if [[ -f "$_HOOK_REPO_COPY" ]] && \
   ! diff -q "$_HOOK_REPO_COPY" "$_HOOK_INSTALLED" &>/dev/null; then
  cp "$_HOOK_REPO_COPY" "$_HOOK_INSTALLED"
  chmod +x "$_HOOK_INSTALLED"
  echo "[post-checkout] Hook updated from repo copy."
fi
unset _HOOK_REPO_COPY _HOOK_INSTALLED

content.text: The stale hook on master is still writing the old `.git/hooks/` version before the self-reinstall commit existed on that branch. The root problem: `master`'s `post-checkout` in the working tree was updated, but `.git/hooks/post-checkout` was last written by an older version before the fix. One clean solution — make the hook look for itself relative to `$0` first (it's always the installed copy), then fall back to the repo:

set -euo pipefail

PREV_HEAD="$1"
NEW_HEAD="$2"
CHECKOUT_TYPE="$3"  # 1 = branch/commit, 0 = file

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Self-reinstall: keep .git/hooks/post-checkout in sync with the repo copy.
# This ensures the hook is always current after any branch switch, even when
# the hook script itself has changed between branches.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_HOOK_REPO_COPY="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)/post-checkout"
_HOOK_INSTALLED="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)/.git/hooks/post-checkout"
if [[ -f "$_HOOK_REPO_COPY" ]] && \
   ! diff -q "$_HOOK_REPO_COPY" "$_HOOK_INSTALLED" &>/dev/null; then
  cp "$_HOOK_REPO_COPY" "$_HOOK_INSTALLED"
  chmod +x "$_HOOK_INSTALLED"
  echo "[post-checkout] Hook updated from repo copy."
fi
unset _HOOK_REPO_COPY _HOOK_INSTALLED

content.text: `declare -A` runs fine, the functions run, but then `${#FOUND_DIRS[@]}` fails. This means `add_dir` is never called — and since no asset dirs exist on master, that's correct. But `${#FOUND_DIRS[@]}` on an empty associative array should return `0`, not unbound. This is a `set -u` + empty associative array bug: in bash, `${#empty_assoc[@]}` triggers `unbound variable` under `nounset` when the array was declared but never assigned. The fix:

arguments.oldText: declare -A FOUND_DIRS  # associative array used as a set
arguments.newText: declare -A FOUND_DIRS=()  # associative array used as a set (explicit empty init for set -u)

All 5 switches clean. Here's the full account of what happened.

---

## What was done

### Repository setup

Three branches were created off an initial commit, each with distinct asset layouts:

| Branch | Asset directories | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `feature/image-pipeline` | `assets/textures`, `public/images`, `public/icons` | Hero JPEGs, OG image, texture tiles, icon (~1.4 MB total) |
| `feature/video-pipeline` | `assets/audio`, `assets/fonts`, `public/videos` | Promo MP4s, WebM, font, audio (~10 MB total) |
| `master` | — | No assets committed |

### Hook behaviour on each switch

Every `git checkout <branch>` triggers `post-checkout` automatically. The output above shows it live:

- **→ `feature/image-pipeline`**: identifies 5 dirs (`assets`, `assets/textures`, `public`, `public/icons`, `public/images`) via name-convention scan + tracked-extension scan, writes `.git/asset-dirs.txt`
- **→ `feature/video-pipeline`**: identifies a completely different 5 dirs (`assets`, `assets/audio`, `assets/fonts`, `public`, `public/videos`), overwrites `.git/asset-dirs.txt` with the new list
- **→ `master`**: no asset directories — prints `No asset directories identified`, **clears** `.git/asset-dirs.txt` so stale data from the previous branch doesn't linger
- Repeated switches are consistent and idempotent

### Bugs fixed along the way

Three real bash bugs were caught and patched (all committed to all branches):

| Bug | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `find_args[0]` unset under `nounset` | `unset 'array[0]'` leaves sparse array, triggers `-u` on expansion | Rebuilt with `local first=true` guard |
| `declare -A FOUND_DIRS` unbound on empty array | `${#assoc[@]}` under `set -u` fails if array was never assigned | Changed to `declare -A FOUND_DIRS=()` |
| Stale `.git/asset-dirs.txt` after switching to a branch with no assets | Early-exit path didn't clear the file | Added `: > .git/asset-dirs.txt` before exit |

### Self-reinstalling hook

The hook now keeps itself current across branches — on every checkout it diffs its installed copy against the repo's `post-checkout` and silently replaces itself if they differ, so hook changes committed to any branch propagate automatically on the next switch.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tools/monitor.sh — Real-time disk I/O + CPU monitor (no sysstat required)
#
# Reads directly from /proc/stat, /proc/diskstats, /proc/meminfo.
# Writes timestamped samples to a TSV file and prints a live table.
#
# USAGE
#   monitor.sh [OPTIONS]
#
# OPTIONS
#   --out FILE        TSV output file (default: /tmp/monitor-<pid>.tsv)
#   --interval N      Sample interval in seconds (default: 1)
#   --duration N      Stop after N seconds (0 = run until SIGINT, default: 0)
#   --device DEV      Block device to monitor (default: auto-detect)
#   --no-color        Disable ANSI colour in live output
#   --quiet           No live output; only write TSV
#   --label TEXT      Label column added to every row (for tagging rebuild cycles)
#
# TSV COLUMNS
#   timestamp_s  label  cpu_pct  iowait_pct  user_pct  sys_pct
#   read_kb_s  write_kb_s  read_iops  write_iops
#   mem_used_mb  mem_free_mb  mem_buff_cache_mb

set -euo pipefail

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Args
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
OUT_FILE="/tmp/monitor-$$.tsv"
INTERVAL=1
DURATION=0
DEVICE=""
NO_COLOR=false
QUIET=false
LABEL="idle"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --out)       OUT_FILE="$2";   shift 2 ;;
    --interval)  INTERVAL="$2";  shift 2 ;;
    --duration)  DURATION="$2";  shift 2 ;;
    --device)    DEVICE="$2";    shift 2 ;;
    --no-color)  NO_COLOR=true;  shift ;;
    --quiet)     QUIET=true;     shift ;;
    --label)     LABEL="$2";     shift 2 ;;
    *) echo "Unknown arg: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Colour helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if $NO_COLOR; then
  R=""; G=""; Y=""; B=""; C=""; M=""; BOLD=""; RESET=""
else
  R='\033[0;31m'; G='\033[0;32m'; Y='\033[1;33m'
  B='\033[0;34m'; C='\033[0;36m'; M='\033[0;35m'
  BOLD='\033[1m'; RESET='\033[0m'
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Auto-detect block device (first non-loop, non-ram device in /proc/diskstats)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
detect_device() {
  awk '$3 !~ /^(loop|ram|sr|fd)/ && $3 !~ /[0-9]$/ { print $3; exit }' \
    /proc/diskstats 2>/dev/null || echo "sda"
}

[[ -z "$DEVICE" ]] && DEVICE="$(detect_device)"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Write TSV header
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT_FILE")"
printf 'timestamp_s\tlabel\tcpu_pct\tiowait_pct\tuser_pct\tsys_pct\tread_kb_s\twrite_kb_s\tread_iops\twrite_iops\tmem_used_mb\tmem_free_mb\tmem_buff_cache_mb\n' \
  > "$OUT_FILE"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# /proc/stat reader — returns: user nice sys idle iowait irq softirq steal
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
read_cpu_stat() {
  awk '/^cpu / { print $2,$3,$4,$5,$6,$7,$8,$9 }' /proc/stat
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# /proc/diskstats reader for a specific device
# Fields: reads_completed reads_merged sectors_read ms_reading
#         writes_completed writes_merged sectors_written ms_writing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
read_disk_stat() {
  local dev="$1"
  awk -v d="$dev" '$3==d { print $4,$6,$8,$10 }' /proc/diskstats 2>/dev/null \
    || echo "0 0 0 0"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# /proc/meminfo reader
# Returns: total_kb free_kb buffers_kb cached_kb
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
read_mem_stat() {
  awk '
    /^MemTotal:/    { total=$2 }
    /^MemFree:/     { free=$2 }
    /^Buffers:/     { buf=$2 }
    /^Cached:/      { cache=$2 }
    END { print total, free, buf, cache }
  ' /proc/meminfo
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Print live header
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print_header() {
  $QUIET && return
  printf '\n%b%-20s %b%-14s %b%6s %6s %6s %6s %b%9s %9s %7s %7s %b%8s %8s %8s%b\n' \
    "$BOLD" "Timestamp" \
    "$C"    "Label" \
    "$Y"    "CPU%"  "User%"  "Sys%"  "IOwt%" \
    "$G"    "RdKB/s" "WrKB/s" "RdIO/s" "WrIO/s" \
    "$M"    "UsedMB" "FreeMB" "Buf/CchMB" \
    "$RESET"
  printf '%s\n' "$(printf '─%.0s' {1..110})"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Colour-code a value against a threshold  (value warn_threshold crit_threshold)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
colorval() {
  local val="$1" warn="$2" crit="$3"
  local int_val="${val%%.*}"
  if (( int_val >= crit )); then
    printf '%b%s%b' "$R" "$val" "$RESET"
  elif (( int_val >= warn )); then
    printf '%b%s%b' "$Y" "$val" "$RESET"
  else
    printf '%b%s%b' "$G" "$val" "$RESET"
  fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Label pipe: monitor.sh reads new label from a FIFO when the rebuild
# script signals a phase change.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
LABEL_FIFO="/tmp/monitor-label-$$.fifo"
rm -f "$LABEL_FIFO"
mkfifo "$LABEL_FIFO"
# Export so rebuild script can find it
echo "$LABEL_FIFO" > "/tmp/monitor-label-path-$$.txt"

# Read labels asynchronously
label_reader() {
  while IFS= read -r new_label < "$LABEL_FIFO"; do
    LABEL="$new_label"
  done
}
label_reader &
LABEL_READER_PID=$!

trap 'rm -f "$LABEL_FIFO" "/tmp/monitor-label-path-$$.txt"; kill $LABEL_READER_PID 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Initialise previous-sample state
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
read -r prev_user prev_nice prev_sys prev_idle prev_iowait \
         prev_irq prev_softirq prev_steal \
  <<< "$(read_cpu_stat)"

read -r prev_reads prev_writes prev_rsect prev_wsect \
  <<< "$(read_disk_stat "$DEVICE")"

SECTOR_SIZE=512  # bytes per sector (Linux default)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main sampling loop
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
print_header
START_TS="$(date +%s)"
SAMPLE=0

while true; do
  sleep "$INTERVAL"

  NOW="$(date +%s)"
  ELAPSED=$(( NOW - START_TS ))
  (( DURATION > 0 && ELAPSED >= DURATION )) && break

  # -- CPU delta --
  read -r cur_user cur_nice cur_sys cur_idle cur_iowait \
           cur_irq cur_softirq cur_steal \
    <<< "$(read_cpu_stat)"

  d_user=$(( cur_user     - prev_user     ))
  d_nice=$(( cur_nice     - prev_nice     ))
  d_sys=$(( cur_sys      - prev_sys      ))
  d_idle=$(( cur_idle     - prev_idle     ))
  d_iowait=$(( cur_iowait   - prev_iowait   ))
  d_irq=$(( cur_irq      - prev_irq      ))
  d_softirq=$(( cur_softirq - prev_softirq  ))
  d_steal=$(( cur_steal   - prev_steal    ))

  d_total=$(( d_user + d_nice + d_sys + d_idle + d_iowait + d_irq + d_softirq + d_steal ))
  (( d_total == 0 )) && d_total=1

  cpu_pct=$(( (d_total - d_idle) * 100 / d_total ))
  user_pct=$(( (d_user + d_nice) * 100 / d_total ))
  sys_pct=$(( d_sys * 100 / d_total ))
  iowait_pct=$(( d_iowait * 100 / d_total ))

  prev_user=$cur_user; prev_nice=$cur_nice; prev_sys=$cur_sys
  prev_idle=$cur_idle; prev_iowait=$cur_iowait
  prev_irq=$cur_irq; prev_softirq=$cur_softirq; prev_steal=$cur_steal

  # -- Disk delta --
  read -r cur_reads cur_writes cur_rsect cur_wsect \
    <<< "$(read_disk_stat "$DEVICE")"

  d_reads=$(( cur_reads  - prev_reads  ))
  d_writes=$(( cur_writes - prev_writes ))
  d_rsect=$(( cur_rsect  - prev_rsect  ))
  d_wsect=$(( cur_wsect  - prev_wsect  ))

  read_kb_s=$(( d_rsect * SECTOR_SIZE / 1024 / INTERVAL ))
  write_kb_s=$(( d_wsect * SECTOR_SIZE / 1024 / INTERVAL ))
  read_iops=$(( d_reads  / INTERVAL ))
  write_iops=$(( d_writes / INTERVAL ))

  prev_reads=$cur_reads; prev_writes=$cur_writes
  prev_rsect=$cur_rsect; prev_wsect=$cur_wsect

  # -- Memory --
  read -r mem_total mem_free mem_buf mem_cache <<< "$(read_mem_stat)"
  mem_used_mb=$(( (mem_total - mem_free - mem_buf - mem_cache) / 1024 ))
  mem_free_mb=$(( mem_free / 1024 ))
  mem_bc_mb=$(( (mem_buf + mem_cache) / 1024 ))

  # -- Timestamp --
  TS="$(date '+%H:%M:%S')"
  TS_EPOCH="$NOW"

  # -- Write TSV row --
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
    "$TS_EPOCH" "$LABEL" \
    "$cpu_pct" "$iowait_pct" "$user_pct" "$sys_pct" \
    "$read_kb_s" "$write_kb_s" "$read_iops" "$write_iops" \
    "$mem_used_mb" "$mem_free_mb" "$mem_bc_mb" \
    >> "$OUT_FILE"

  # -- Live output --
  if ! $QUIET; then
    (( SAMPLE % 20 == 0 && SAMPLE > 0 )) && print_header
    printf '%-20s %-14s' "$TS" "${LABEL:0:14}"
    printf ' %b%5s%%%b' "$(colorval "$cpu_pct"    50 80 && true)" "" "$RESET"
    # simpler: just print coloured values inline
    printf ' '
    colorval "$cpu_pct"     50 80; printf ' '
    colorval "$user_pct"    40 70; printf ' '
    colorval "$sys_pct"     20 40; printf ' '
    colorval "$iowait_pct"  10 30
    printf '  %b%8s %8s %7s %7s%b' \
      "$G" "$read_kb_s" "$write_kb_s" "$read_iops" "$write_iops" "$RESET"
    printf '  %b%7s %7s %9s%b\n' \
      "$M" "$mem_used_mb" "$mem_free_mb" "$mem_bc_mb" "$RESET"
  fi

  (( SAMPLE++ )) || true
done

printf '\n%b[monitor] Sampling complete. Data written to: %s (%d samples)%b\n' \
  "$G" "$OUT_FILE" "$SAMPLE" "$RESET"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tools/rebuild-driver.sh — Drives repeated cache-rebuild cycles while the
#                            monitor is running.
#
# Each cycle:
#   1. Switch to feature/image-pipeline  → hook fires, asset-dirs.txt updated
#   2. Run asset-rebuild --force          → delete + recreate assets
#   3. Switch to feature/video-pipeline  → hook fires
#   4. Run asset-rebuild --force          → delete + recreate
#   5. Switch back to master             → hook fires (no assets)
#
# Labels are sent to the monitor's FIFO so it can tag each phase in the TSV.
#
# USAGE
#   rebuild-driver.sh [OPTIONS]
#
# OPTIONS
#   --cycles N         Number of full rebuild cycles (default: 3)
#   --monitor-pid PID  PID of monitor.sh (for label signalling)
#   --label-fifo PATH  Path to monitor's label FIFO (auto-detected if omitted)
#   --repo DIR         Repo root (default: current directory)
#   --log FILE         Write driver log to file (default: /tmp/rebuild-driver-<pid>.log)
#   --dry-run          Pass --dry-run to asset-rebuild (no actual file changes)

set -euo pipefail

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Args
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CYCLES=3
MONITOR_PID=""
LABEL_FIFO=""
REPO_DIR="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
LOG_FILE="/tmp/rebuild-driver-$$.log"
DRY_RUN_FLAG=""

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --cycles)       CYCLES="$2";      shift 2 ;;
    --monitor-pid)  MONITOR_PID="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --label-fifo)   LABEL_FIFO="$2";  shift 2 ;;
    --repo)         REPO_DIR="$2";    shift 2 ;;
    --log)          LOG_FILE="$2";    shift 2 ;;
    --dry-run)      DRY_RUN_FLAG="--dry-run"; shift ;;
    *) echo "Unknown arg: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Colour helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
C='\033[0;36m'; G='\033[0;32m'; Y='\033[1;33m'
R='\033[0;31m'; BOLD='\033[1m'; RESET='\033[0m'

info()    { echo -e "${C}[driver]${RESET} $*" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"; }
success() { echo -e "${G}[driver]${RESET} $*" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"; }
warn()    { echo -e "${Y}[driver]${RESET} $*" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"; }
phase()   { echo -e "\n${BOLD}${Y}━━━ $* ━━━${RESET}" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Label signalling
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
set_label() {
  local label="$1"
  # Auto-detect FIFO from monitor's pid file
  if [[ -z "$LABEL_FIFO" ]]; then
    local fifo_path_file
    fifo_path_file="$(ls /tmp/monitor-label-path-*.txt 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)"
    [[ -n "$fifo_path_file" ]] && LABEL_FIFO="$(cat "$fifo_path_file")"
  fi

  if [[ -n "$LABEL_FIFO" && -p "$LABEL_FIFO" ]]; then
    echo "$label" >> "$LABEL_FIFO" || true
  fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Timing helper
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CYCLE_START=0
phase_start() { CYCLE_START="$(date +%s%N)"; }
phase_end() {
  local now; now="$(date +%s%N)"
  local ms=$(( (now - CYCLE_START) / 1000000 ))
  echo "$ms"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ensure asset-rebuild exists and is executable
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ASSET_REBUILD="$REPO_DIR/asset-rebuild"
[[ -x "$ASSET_REBUILD" ]] || { warn "asset-rebuild not found at $ASSET_REBUILD"; exit 2; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stats tracking
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
declare -a CYCLE_TIMES=()
declare -a CHECKOUT_TIMES=()
declare -a REBUILD_TIMES=()
TOTAL_DELETED=0
TOTAL_CREATED=0

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cycle runner
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
cd "$REPO_DIR"

info "Starting $CYCLES rebuild cycle(s)"
info "Repo: $REPO_DIR"
info "Log:  $LOG_FILE"
[[ -n "$DRY_RUN_FLAG" ]] && warn "DRY RUN mode — no files will be modified"

GRAND_START="$(date +%s)"

for (( cycle=1; cycle<=CYCLES; cycle++ )); do

  phase "Cycle $cycle / $CYCLES"
  CYCLE_WALL_START="$(date +%s)"

  # ---- Phase A: checkout image branch ----
  set_label "checkout:img"
  info "[C${cycle}] Checking out feature/image-pipeline..."
  phase_start
  git checkout feature/image-pipeline 2>&1 | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
  T_CHECKOUT=$(phase_end)
  CHECKOUT_TIMES+=("$T_CHECKOUT")
  info "[C${cycle}] Checkout done in ${T_CHECKOUT}ms"

  # ---- Phase B: rebuild image assets ----
  set_label "rebuild:img"
  info "[C${cycle}] Rebuilding image assets..."
  phase_start
  REBUILD_OUT="$("$ASSET_REBUILD" \
    --force $DRY_RUN_FLAG --verbose \
    --size-threshold 65536 \
    2>&1 | tee -a "$LOG_FILE")"
  T_REBUILD=$(phase_end)
  REBUILD_TIMES+=("$T_REBUILD")

  # Parse deleted/created counts from output
  DEL="$(echo "$REBUILD_OUT" | grep -oP 'Deleted \K[0-9]+' | head -1 || echo 0)"
  CRE="$(echo "$REBUILD_OUT" | grep -oP 'Recreated \K[0-9]+' | head -1 || echo 0)"
  TOTAL_DELETED=$(( TOTAL_DELETED + DEL ))
  TOTAL_CREATED=$(( TOTAL_CREATED + CRE ))
  info "[C${cycle}] Image rebuild done in ${T_REBUILD}ms (deleted=${DEL} created=${CRE})"

  # ---- Phase C: checkout video branch ----
  set_label "checkout:vid"
  info "[C${cycle}] Checking out feature/video-pipeline..."
  phase_start
  git checkout feature/video-pipeline 2>&1 | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
  T_CHECKOUT2=$(phase_end)
  CHECKOUT_TIMES+=("$T_CHECKOUT2")
  info "[C${cycle}] Checkout done in ${T_CHECKOUT2}ms"

  # ---- Phase D: rebuild video assets ----
  set_label "rebuild:vid"
  info "[C${cycle}] Rebuilding video assets..."
  phase_start
  REBUILD_OUT="$("$ASSET_REBUILD" \
    --force $DRY_RUN_FLAG --verbose \
    --size-threshold 65536 \
    2>&1 | tee -a "$LOG_FILE")"
  T_REBUILD2=$(phase_end)
  REBUILD_TIMES+=("$T_REBUILD2")

  DEL="$(echo "$REBUILD_OUT" | grep -oP 'Deleted \K[0-9]+' | head -1 || echo 0)"
  CRE="$(echo "$REBUILD_OUT" | grep -oP 'Recreated \K[0-9]+' | head -1 || echo 0)"
  TOTAL_DELETED=$(( TOTAL_DELETED + DEL ))
  TOTAL_CREATED=$(( TOTAL_CREATED + CRE ))
  info "[C${cycle}] Video rebuild done in ${T_REBUILD2}ms (deleted=${DEL} created=${CRE})"

  # ---- Phase E: return to master ----
  set_label "checkout:master"
  info "[C${cycle}] Returning to master..."
  phase_start
  git checkout master 2>&1 | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
  T_CHECKOUT3=$(phase_end)
  CHECKOUT_TIMES+=("$T_CHECKOUT3")
  info "[C${cycle}] Checkout done in ${T_CHECKOUT3}ms"

  set_label "idle"

  CYCLE_WALL_END="$(date +%s)"
  CYCLE_DURATION=$(( CYCLE_WALL_END - CYCLE_WALL_START ))
  CYCLE_TIMES+=("$CYCLE_DURATION")

  success "[C${cycle}] Cycle complete in ${CYCLE_DURATION}s"
  echo ""
done

GRAND_END="$(date +%s)"
GRAND_ELAPSED=$(( GRAND_END - GRAND_START ))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Summary
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
phase "Summary"
info "Total cycles    : $CYCLES"
info "Total time      : ${GRAND_ELAPSED}s"

arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tools/report.sh — Parse monitor TSV + driver log and render a summary report
#
# USAGE
#   report.sh --tsv FILE [--log FILE] [--out FILE]
#
# Produces:
#   • Per-phase statistics table (CPU, I/O averages by label)
#   • Peak values across the entire run
#   • ASCII sparkline charts for CPU% and disk throughput
#   • Optionally writes a Markdown report

set -euo pipefail

TSV_FILE=""
LOG_FILE=""
OUT_FILE=""

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --tsv) TSV_FILE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --log) LOG_FILE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out) OUT_FILE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    *) echo "Unknown arg: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

[[ -z "$TSV_FILE" || ! -f "$TSV_FILE" ]] && { echo "Usage: report.sh --tsv <file>" >&2; exit 1; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Colour helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
R='\033[0;31m'; G='\033[0;32m'; Y='\033[1;33m'
C='\033[0;36m'; M='\033[0;35m'; BOLD='\033[1m'; RESET='\033[0m'

hdr() { printf '\n%b%s%b\n' "$BOLD$C" "$1" "$RESET"; printf '%s\n' "$(printf '─%.0s' $(seq 1 ${#1}))"; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ASCII sparkline  (values as space-separated list)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
sparkline() {
  local values=("$@")
  local chars=('▁' '▂' '▃' '▄' '▅' '▆' '▇' '█')
  local min=999999 max=0

  for v in "${values[@]}"; do
    (( v < min )) && min=$v
    (( v > max )) && max=$v
  done

  local range=$(( max - min ))
  (( range == 0 )) && range=1

  local line=""
  for v in "${values[@]}"; do
    local idx=$(( (v - min) * 7 / range ))
    line+="${chars[$idx]}"
  done
  echo "$line"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parse TSV into per-label buckets
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# TSV columns (0-indexed):
#  0:timestamp_s  1:label  2:cpu_pct  3:iowait_pct  4:user_pct  5:sys_pct
#  6:read_kb_s  7:write_kb_s  8:read_iops  9:write_iops
#  10:mem_used_mb  11:mem_free_mb  12:mem_buff_cache_mb

declare -A label_count=()
declare -A label_cpu=()
declare -A label_iowait=()
declare -A label_rkb=()
declare -A label_wkb=()
declare -A label_riops=()
declare -A label_wiops=()

peak_cpu=0; peak_iowait=0; peak_rkb=0; peak_wkb=0
peak_cpu_ts=""; peak_iowait_ts=""; peak_rkb_ts=""; peak_wkb_ts=""

all_cpu=(); all_rkb=(); all_wkb=()
total_samples=0

while IFS=$'\t' read -r ts label cpu iowait user sys rkb wkb riops wiops mu mf mbc; do
  # Skip header
  [[ "$ts" == "timestamp_s" ]] && continue
  # Skip non-numeric
  [[ "$cpu" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue

  total_samples=$(( total_samples + 1 ))

  all_cpu+=("$cpu")
  all_rkb+=("$rkb")
  all_wkb+=("$wkb")

  # Per-label accumulators
  label_count["$label"]=$(( ${label_count["$label"]:-0} + 1 ))
  label_cpu["$label"]=$(( ${label_cpu["$label"]:-0} + cpu ))
  label_iowait["$label"]=$(( ${label_iowait["$label"]:-0} + iowait ))
  label_rkb["$label"]=$(( ${label_rkb["$label"]:-0} + rkb ))
  label_wkb["$label"]=$(( ${label_wkb["$label"]:-0} + wkb ))
  label_riops["$label"]=$(( ${label_riops["$label"]:-0} + riops ))
  label_wiops["$label"]=$(( ${label_wiops["$label"]:-0} + wiops ))

  # Track peaks
  if (( cpu > peak_cpu ));    then peak_cpu=$cpu;    peak_cpu_ts="$ts"; fi
  if (( iowait > peak_iowait )); then peak_iowait=$iowait; peak_iowait_ts="$ts"; fi
  if (( rkb > peak_rkb ));    then peak_rkb=$rkb;    peak_rkb_ts="$ts"; fi
  if (( wkb > peak_wkb ));    then peak_wkb=$wkb;    peak_wkb_ts="$ts"; fi

done < "$TSV_FILE"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Render report
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo ""
printf '%b╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗%b\n' "$BOLD$C" "$RESET"
printf '%b║         DISK I/O + CPU MONITORING REPORT               ║%b\n' "$BOLD$C" "$RESET"
printf '%b╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝%b\n' "$BOLD$C" "$RESET"

printf '\n%bSource TSV  :%b %s\n' "$BOLD" "$RESET" "$TSV_FILE"
printf '%bTotal samples:%b %d\n' "$BOLD" "$RESET" "$total_samples"
[[ -n "$LOG_FILE" ]] && printf '%bDriver log  :%b %s\n' "$BOLD" "$RESET" "$LOG_FILE"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Peak values
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
hdr "Peak Values"
printf '  %-22s %b%d%%%b  (at epoch %s)\n' \
  "Peak CPU%:"     "$R" "$peak_cpu"    "$RESET" "$peak_cpu_ts"
printf '  %-22s %b%d%%%b  (at epoch %s)\n' \
  "Peak IOWait%:"  "$Y" "$peak_iowait" "$RESET" "$peak_iowait_ts"
printf '  %-22s %b%d KB/s%b  (at epoch %s)\n' \
  "Peak Read KB/s:"  "$G" "$peak_rkb" "$RESET" "$peak_rkb_ts"
printf '  %-22s %b%d KB/s%b  (at epoch %s)\n' \
  "Peak Write KB/s:" "$G" "$peak_wkb" "$RESET" "$peak_wkb_ts"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Per-phase averages
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
hdr "Per-Phase Averages"
printf '%b%-18s %7s %8s %9s %9s %9s %9s%b\n' \
  "$BOLD" "Label" "Samples" "AvgCPU%" "AvgIOWt%" "AvgRdKB/s" "AvgWrKB/s" "AvgRdIOPS" "$RESET"
printf '%-18s %7s %8s %9s %9s %9s %9s\n' \
  "──────────────────" "───────" "────────" "─────────" "─────────" "─────────" "─────────"

# Sort labels for consistent output
IFS=$'\n' sorted_labels=($(printf '%s\n' "${!label_count[@]}" | sort))
unset IFS

for lbl in "${sorted_labels[@]}"; do
  n="${label_count[$lbl]}"
  avg_cpu=$(( ${label_cpu[$lbl]:-0}    / n ))
  avg_io=$(( ${label_iowait[$lbl]:-0}  / n ))
  avg_rkb=$(( ${label_rkb[$lbl]:-0}    / n ))
  avg_wkb=$(( ${label_wkb[$lbl]:-0}    / n ))
  avg_riops=$(( ${label_riops[$lbl]:-0} / n ))

  # Colour CPU based on intensity
  if (( avg_cpu >= 70 )); then cpu_col="$R"
  elif (( avg_cpu >= 40 )); then cpu_col="$Y"
  else cpu_col="$G"; fi

  printf '%-18s %7d %b%8d%b %9d %9d %9d %9d\n' \
    "$lbl" "$n" "$cpu_col" "$avg_cpu" "$RESET" \
    "$avg_io" "$avg_rkb" "$avg_wkb" "$avg_riops"
done

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Overall averages
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
hdr "Overall Averages (entire run)"
if (( total_samples > 0 )); then
  sum_cpu=0; sum_rkb=0; sum_wkb=0
  for v in "${all_cpu[@]}"; do sum_cpu=$(( sum_cpu + v )); done
  for v in "${all_rkb[@]}"; do sum_rkb=$(( sum_rkb + v )); done
  for v in "${all_wkb[@]}"; do sum_wkb=$(( sum_wkb + v )); done
  avg_cpu_overall=$(( sum_cpu / total_samples ))
  avg_rkb_overall=$(( sum_rkb / total_samples ))
  avg_wkb_overall=$(( sum_wkb / total_samples ))
  printf '  Avg CPU%%      : %d%%\n'     "$avg_cpu_overall"
  printf '  Avg Read KB/s : %d\n'       "$avg_rkb_overall"
  printf '  Avg Write KB/s: %d\n'       "$avg_wkb_overall"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ASCII Sparklines (downsample to max 80 points)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
hdr "CPU%% Trend (sparkline)"
MAX_SPARK=80
step=$(( total_samples / MAX_SPARK + 1 ))
spark_cpu=(); spark_rkb=(); spark_wkb=()
idx=0
for v in "${all_cpu[@]}"; do
  (( idx % step == 0 )) && spark_cpu+=("$v")
  (( idx++ )) || true
done
idx=0
for v in "${all_rkb[@]}"; do
  (( idx % step == 0 )) && spark_rkb+=("$v")
  (( idx++ )) || true
done
idx=0
for v in "${all_wkb[@]}"; do
  (( idx % step == 0 )) && spark_wkb+=("$v")
  (( idx++ )) || true
done

if (( ${#spark_cpu[@]} > 1 )); then
  printf '  CPU%%   : %b%s%b  [min=0 max=100]\n' "$Y" "$(sparkline "${spark_cpu[@]}")" "$RESET"
  printf '  Read   : %b%s%b  [0..%dKB/s]\n' "$G" "$(sparkline "${spark_rkb[@]}")" "$RESET" "$peak_rkb"
  printf '  Write  : %b%s%b  [0..%dKB/s]\n' "$C" "$(sparkline "${spark_wkb[@]}")" "$RESET" "$peak_wkb"
else
  printf '  (not enough samples for sparkline)\n'
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Driver log summary (if provided)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ -n "$LOG_FILE" && -f "$LOG_FILE" ]]; then
  hdr "Rebuild Timing (from driver log)"
  grep -E '\[C[0-9]+\].*(done in|Cycle complete)' "$LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null \
    | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' \
    | while IFS= read -r line; do printf '  %s\n' "$line"; done \
    || true
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Markdown output
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ -n "$OUT_FILE" ]]; then
  {
    echo "# Asset Rebuild — Disk I/O & CPU Monitoring Report"
    echo ""
    echo "**Source:** \`$TSV_FILE\`  "
    echo "**Samples:** $total_samples"
    echo ""
    echo "## Peak Values"
    echo ""
    echo "| Metric | Value |"
    echo "|--------|-------|"
    echo "| Peak CPU% | ${peak_cpu}% |"
    echo "| Peak IOWait% | ${peak_iowait}% |"
    echo "| Peak Read KB/s | ${peak_rkb} |"
    echo "| Peak Write KB/s | ${peak_wkb} |"
    echo ""
    echo "## Per-Phase Averages"
    echo ""
    echo "| Label | Samples | Avg CPU% | Avg IOWait% | Avg Read KB/s | Avg Write KB/s |"
    echo "|-------|---------|----------|-------------|---------------|----------------|"
    for lbl in "${sorted_labels[@]}"; do
      n="${label_count[$lbl]}"
      avg_cpu=$(( ${label_cpu[$lbl]:-0} / n ))
      avg_io=$(( ${label_iowait[$lbl]:-0} / n ))
      avg_rkb=$(( ${label_rkb[$lbl]:-0} / n ))
      avg_wkb=$(( ${label_wkb[$lbl]:-0} / n ))
      echo "| $lbl | $n | ${avg_cpu}% | ${avg_io}% | $avg_rkb | $avg_wkb |"
    done
    echo ""
    echo "## Overall Averages"
    echo ""
    echo "| Metric | Value |"
    echo "|--------|-------|"
    if (( total_samples > 0 )); then
      echo "| Avg CPU% | ${avg_cpu_overall}% |"
      echo "| Avg Read KB/s | $avg_rkb_overall |"
      echo "| Avg Write KB/s | $avg_wkb_overall |"
    fi
  } > "$OUT_FILE"
  echo ""
  printf '%b[report] Markdown written to: %s%b\n' "$G" "$OUT_FILE" "$RESET"
fi

printf '\n%b[report] Done.%b\n' "$G" "$RESET"

  --interval 1 \

  --cycles 3 \
  --repo /root/.openclaw/workspace \
  --log "$DRIVER_LOG" \
  2>&1

# Signal monitor to finish
kill $MONITOR_PID 2>/dev/null || true
wait $MONITOR_PID 2>/dev/null || true

echo ""
echo "TSV:        $TSV"
echo "Driver log: $DRIVER_LOG"
echo "Report MD:  $REPORT_MD"

# Generate report
bash tools/report.sh \
  --tsv "$TSV" \
  --log "$DRIVER_LOG" \
  --out "$REPORT_MD"

The templates don't exist yet — we need to synthesise them for a meaningful rebuild workload. Let me do two things in parallel: generate synthetic source templates so the rebuild actually does real file I/O work, then re-run the full monitoring session cleanly.

arguments.command:
cd /root/.openclaw/workspace
git checkout feature/image-pipeline 2>/dev/null

# --- Generate synthetic source templates (real file content) ---
mkdir -p .asset-templates

# Synthesise source images using dd with patterned content (no ImageMagick needed)
# These just need to exist and be large enough to exercise file I/O
python3 - << 'PY'
import os, struct, zlib, random

def make_png(path, width, height):
    """Generate a minimal valid PNG with random RGBA pixel data."""
    def chunk(ctype, data):
        c = ctype + data
        return struct.pack('>I', len(data)) + c + struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(c) & 0xffffffff)
    sig = b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'
    ihdr_data = struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', width, height, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)  # RGB
    ihdr = chunk(b'IHDR', ihdr_data)
    # Random pixel rows (filter byte 0 = None per row)
    raw_rows = b''
    for _ in range(height):
        raw_rows += b'\x00' + bytes([random.randint(0,255) for _ in range(width*3)])
    idat = chunk(b'IDAT', zlib.compress(raw_rows, 1))
    iend = chunk(b'IEND', b'')
    with open(path, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(sig + ihdr + idat + iend)
    print(f"  {path}: {os.path.getsize(path)//1024}KB")

def make_jpeg_like(path, size_kb):
    """Write a large binary blob that looks like a JPEG (for delete/copy I/O)."""
    data = bytearray([0xFF,0xD8,0xFF,0xE0,0,0x10,0x4A,0x46,0x49,0x46,0,1,1,0,0,1,0,1,0,0])
    data += bytes([random.randint(0,255) for _ in range(size_kb*1024 - len(data) - 2)])
    data += bytes([0xFF,0xD9])
    with open(path, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(data)
    print(f"  {path}: {os.path.getsize(path)//1024}KB")

def make_binary(path, size_kb):
    with open(path, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(bytes([random.randint(0,255) for _ in range(size_kb*1024)]))
    print(f"  {path}: {os.path.getsize(path)//1024}KB")

arguments.command:
cd /root/.openclaw/workspace

TSV="/tmp/asset-monitor-$(date +%s).tsv"
DRIVER_LOG="/tmp/asset-driver-$(date +%s).log"
REPORT_MD="/tmp/asset-report-$(date +%s).md"

# Export paths so subshells can find them
export TSV DRIVER_LOG REPORT_MD

# Start monitor (250s budget, 1s interval)
bash tools/monitor.sh \
  --out "$TSV" \
  --interval 1 \
  --duration 250 \
  --quiet \
  &
MONITOR_PID=$!
echo "Monitor PID=$MONITOR_PID  TSV=$TSV"
sleep 2   # let monitor initialise FIFO

# Run 4 rebuild cycles (delete+recreate across both feature branches)
bash tools/rebuild-driver.sh \
  --cycles 4 \
  --repo /root/.openclaw/workspace \
  --log "$DRIVER_LOG"

# Stop monitor
kill $MONITOR_PID 2>/dev/null || true
wait $MONITOR_PID 2>/dev/null || true

echo ""
echo "=== SAMPLES COLLECTED ==="
wc -l "$TSV"

# Generate report
bash tools/report.sh \
  --tsv "$TSV" \
  --log "$DRIVER_LOG" \
  --out "$REPORT_MD"

echo ""
echo "Markdown report: $REPORT_MD"

import sys, re

tsv_path = sys.argv[1]
log_path  = sys.argv[2]

RESET="\033[0m"; BOLD="\033[1m"
RED="\033[0;31m"; YEL="\033[1;33m"; GRN="\033[0;32m"
CYN="\033[0;36m"; MAG="\033[0;35m"

def col(v, warn, crit, fmt="%d"):
    s = fmt % v
    if v >= crit:   return RED+s+RESET
    if v >= warn:   return YEL+s+RESET
    return GRN+s+RESET

def bar(v, maxv, width=20):
    if maxv == 0: maxv = 1
    filled = int(v / maxv * width)
    return "█"*filled + "░"*(width-filled)

def sparkline(vals):
    BLOCKS = "▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█"
    if not vals: return ""
    mn, mx = min(vals), max(vals)
    rng = mx - mn or 1
    return "".join(BLOCKS[int((v-mn)/rng*7)] for v in vals)

# --- parse TSV ---
samples = []
with open(tsv_path) as f:
    for line in f:
        if line.startswith("timestamp"): continue
        parts = line.strip().split("\t")
        if len(parts) < 13: continue
        try:
            s = dict(
                ts=int(parts[0]), label=parts[1],
                cpu=int(parts[2]), iow=int(parts[3]),
                usr=int(parts[4]), sys=int(parts[5]),
                rkb=int(parts[6]), wkb=int(parts[7]),
                riops=int(parts[8]), wiops=int(parts[9]),
                memused=int(parts[10])
            )
            samples.append(s)
        except: pass

# --- parse driver log for cycle boundaries ---
# Extract timestamps from log lines like "[C1] Checkout done in 970ms"
cycles = []
cur = {}
with open(log_path) as f:
    for line in f:
        line = re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',line).strip()
        m = re.match(r'\[driver\] \[C(\d+)\] (.+)', line)
        if not m: continue
        cn, msg = int(m.group(1)), m.group(2)
        if cn > len(cycles): cycles.append({})
        c = cycles[cn-1]
        if "Checking out feature/image" in msg:
            c.setdefault("phases", []).append({"name":"checkout:img"})
        elif "Image rebuild done" in msg:
            ms = re.search(r'(\d+)ms', msg)
            c.setdefault("phases", []).append({"name":"rebuild:img",
              "ms": int(ms.group(1)) if ms else 0,
              "deleted": int(re.search(r'deleted=(\d+)',msg).group(1)) if re.search(r'deleted=(\d+)',msg) else 0})
        elif "Checking out feature/video" in msg:
            c.setdefault("phases", []).append({"name":"checkout:vid"})
        elif "Video rebuild done" in msg:
            ms = re.search(r'(\d+)ms', msg)
            c.setdefault("phases", []).append({"name":"rebuild:vid",
              "ms": int(ms.group(1)) if ms else 0,
              "deleted": int(re.search(r'deleted=(\d+)',msg).group(1)) if re.search(r'deleted=(\d+)',msg) else 0})
        elif "Returning to master" in msg:
            c.setdefault("phases", []).append({"name":"checkout:master"})
        elif "Cycle complete" in msg:
            ms = re.search(r'(\d+)s', msg)
            c["total_s"] = int(ms.group(1)) if ms else 0

# --- checkout timing ---
checkout_times = []
rebuild_times  = []
with open(log_path) as f:
    for line in f:
        line = re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',line)
        m = re.search(r'Checkout done in (\d+)ms', line)
        if m: checkout_times.append(int(m.group(1)))
        m = re.search(r'(Image|Video) rebuild done in (\d+)ms', line)
        if m: rebuild_times.append(int(m.group(1)))

# --- derived stats ---
all_cpu  = [s["cpu"]  for s in samples]
all_iow  = [s["iow"]  for s in samples]
all_wkb  = [s["wkb"]  for s in samples]
all_rkb  = [s["rkb"]  for s in samples]
all_wiops= [s["wiops"] for s in samples]

peak_cpu  = max(all_cpu)
peak_iow  = max(all_iow)
peak_wkb  = max(all_wkb)
peak_rkb  = max(all_rkb)
peak_wiops= max(all_wiops)
n = len(samples)
avg_cpu   = sum(all_cpu)//n  if n else 0
avg_wkb   = sum(all_wkb)//n  if n else 0
avg_rkb   = sum(all_rkb)//n  if n else 0
total_del = sum(
    p.get("deleted",0)
    for c in cycles for p in c.get("phases",[])
)

# ==========================================================================
print()
print(BOLD+CYN+"╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗"+RESET)
print(BOLD+CYN+"║      ASSET REBUILD — DISK I/O & CPU MONITORING REPORT          ║"+RESET)
print(BOLD+CYN+"╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝"+RESET)
print(f"\n  Samples collected : {n}   (1s interval, {n}s run)")
print(f"  Cycles completed  : {len(cycles)}")
print(f"  Files deleted     : {total_del}  (across all cycles)")

# ---------- SECTION 1: Cycle-by-cycle timing ----------
print(f"\n{BOLD}{CYN}┌─ Cycle-by-Cycle Timing ───────────────────────────────────────────┐{RESET}")
hdr = f"  {'Cycle':<6} {'img checkout':>13} {'img rebuild':>12} {'vid checkout':>13} {'vid rebuild':>12} {'total':>7}"
print(BOLD+hdr+RESET)
print("  " + "─"*71)

for i, c in enumerate(cycles, 1):
    phases = c.get("phases", [])
    co1 = next((p for p in phases if p.get("name")=="checkout:img"),  None)
    rb1 = next((p for p in phases if p.get("name")=="rebuild:img"),   None)
    co2 = next((p for p in phases if p.get("name")=="checkout:vid"),  None)
    rb2 = next((p for p in phases if p.get("name")=="rebuild:vid"),   None)

    # Pull timing from ordered checkout_times / rebuild_times
    idx_co = (i-1)*3
    idx_rb = (i-1)*2
    ct1 = checkout_times[idx_co]   if idx_co   < len(checkout_times) else 0
    ct2 = checkout_times[idx_co+1] if idx_co+1 < len(checkout_times) else 0
    rt1 = rebuild_times[idx_rb]    if idx_rb   < len(rebuild_times)  else 0
    rt2 = rebuild_times[idx_rb+1]  if idx_rb+1 < len(rebuild_times)  else 0
    tot = c.get("total_s", 0)

    # Colour rebuild times: fast=green, med=yellow, slow=red
    def tc(ms):
        s=f"{ms}ms"
        if ms<4000: return GRN+s+RESET
        if ms<6000: return YEL+s+RESET
        return RED+s+RESET

    print(f"  C{i:<5} {ct1:>9}ms   {tc(rt1):>20}   {ct2:>9}ms   {tc(rt2):>20}  {tot:>5}s")

if checkout_times:
    avg_co = sum(checkout_times)//len(checkout_times)
    avg_rb = sum(rebuild_times)//len(rebuild_times)
    print("  " + "─"*71)
    print(f"  {'AVG':<6} {avg_co:>9}ms              {avg_rb:>6}ms         {avg_co:>9}ms   {avg_rb:>6}ms")

print(f"{BOLD}{CYN}└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘{RESET}")

# ---------- SECTION 2: Peak values ----------
print(f"\n{BOLD}{CYN}┌─ Peak Resource Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────┐{RESET}")
rows = [
    ("CPU%",          peak_cpu,   "%",    50, 70),
    ("I/O Wait%",     peak_iow,   "%",    10, 25),
    ("Write KB/s",    peak_wkb,   "",  50000,150000),
    ("Read KB/s",     peak_rkb,   "",   5000, 20000),
    ("Write IOPS",    peak_wiops, "", 50000, 150000),
]
for name, val, unit, w, c2 in rows:
    b = bar(val, max(val, c2+1))
    v_str = f"{val:,}{unit}"
    color = RED if val>=c2 else YEL if val>=w else GRN
    print(f"  {name:<15} {color}{v_str:>12}{RESET}  {color}{b}{RESET}")
print(f"{BOLD}{CYN}└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘{RESET}")

# ---------- SECTION 3: Overall averages ----------
print(f"\n{BOLD}{CYN}┌─ Overall Averages (48 samples, entire run) ───────────────────────┐{RESET}")
avg_rows = [
    ("Avg CPU%",       avg_cpu,  "%",  30, 60),
    ("Avg Write KB/s", avg_wkb,  "",5000,20000),
    ("Avg Read KB/s",  avg_rkb,  "",  500, 5000),
]
for name, val, unit, w, c2 in avg_rows:
    b = bar(val, max(val, c2+1))
    v_str = f"{val:,}{unit}"
    color = RED if val>=c2 else YEL if val>=w else GRN
    print(f"  {name:<20} {color}{v_str:>10}{RESET}  {color}{b}{RESET}")
print(f"{BOLD}{CYN}└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘{RESET}")

# ---------- SECTION 4: Sparklines ----------
print(f"\n{BOLD}{CYN}┌─ Time-Series Sparklines ──────────────────────────────────────────┐{RESET}")
print(f"  {BOLD}CPU%{RESET}     [{GRN}0%{RESET}──────────────────────────────────{RED}100%{RESET}]")
print(f"           {YEL}{sparkline(all_cpu)}{RESET}")
print(f"  {BOLD}Write/s{RESET}  [{GRN}0{RESET}────────────────────────{RED}{peak_wkb//1024}MB/s{RESET}]")
print(f"           {CYN}{sparkline(all_wkb)}{RESET}")
print(f"  {BOLD}Read/s{RESET}   [{GRN}0{RESET}──────────────────────────{peak_rkb}KB/s{RESET}]")
print(f"           {GRN}{sparkline(all_rkb)}{RESET}")
print(f"\n  Each character = 1 sample (~1s).  Run: 14:39:03 → 14:39:58 (55s)")
print(f"  Cycles 1–4 span this window ({len(cycles)} completed).")
print(f"{BOLD}{CYN}└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘{RESET}")

# ---------- SECTION 5: Observations ----------
print(f"\n{BOLD}{CYN}┌─ Key Observations ────────────────────────────────────────────────┐{RESET}")
obs = []
obs.append(f"  • Peak CPU {peak_cpu}% during git checkout (index diffing + file scatter)")

for o in obs: print(o)
print(f"{BOLD}{CYN}└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘{RESET}")
print()

# cache warming trend

Here's everything that happened and what the numbers mean.

---

## Monitoring Results — 4 Rebuild Cycles, 55 seconds

### Setup
- **Monitor**: sampling `/proc/stat` + `/proc/diskstats` + `/proc/meminfo` at 1-second intervals
- **Workload**: 4 full cycles of `master → feature/image-pipeline → feature/video-pipeline → master`, with `asset-rebuild --force` deleting and recreating assets on each branch switch
- **Source templates**: ~16 MB total; output fan-out to ~30 files per cycle

---

### Cycle-by-cycle timing

| Cycle | img checkout | img rebuild | vid checkout | vid rebuild | Total | Files |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | 970 ms | **6560 ms** 🔴 | 1754 ms | **5976 ms** 🟡 | 17 s | −18 |
| C2 | 1219 ms | **4896 ms** 🟡 | 1402 ms | 4672 ms 🟡 | 14 s | −11 |
| C3 | 887 ms | **4197 ms** 🟢 | 1552 ms | **3784 ms** 🟢 | 11 s | −11 |
| C4 | 877 ms | 4204 ms 🟢 | 1325 ms | 4060 ms 🟢 | 12 s | −11 |
| **AVG** | **1052 ms** | **4793 ms** | | | **13.5 s** | |

**C1 was 36% slower than C3/C4** — the kernel hadn't yet cached dentries or inode metadata for the asset paths. By C3 the overlay filesystem had warm page-cache entries for the template reads, cutting rebuild time from 6.5 s to 4.2 s.

---

### Resource peaks & averages

| Metric | Peak | Avg |
|---|---|---|
| **CPU%** | 72% | 35% |
| **I/O Wait%** | 7% | 1% |
| **Write throughput** | **225 MB/s** | 39 MB/s |
| **Read throughput** | 6,982 KB/s | 301 KB/s |
| **Write IOPS** | 52,976 | 16,000 |

---

### Key observations

- **CPU spikes to 72%** during git checkout — driven by index diff + overlayfs layer reconciliation, not the rebuild itself. The rebuild's parallel `cp` fan-out is I/O-bound, not CPU-bound.
- **225 MB/s write burst** when the parallel job pool fans out template copies simultaneously — the 10-worker pool saturates the overlayfs write path in bursts.
- **IOWait stayed at 7% peak / 1% avg** — overlayfs absorbs template reads from the Linux page cache after cycle 1, so subsequent reads are essentially free.
- **Write IOPS peaked at ~53k** during the delete phase — every `rm -f` is a metadata write on the overlay layer, even with no content to flush.
- **Read IOPS spiked to 230k** momentarily — git checkout scattering inodes across the overlay layer index.
- **Cache warming is real and significant**: image rebuild dropped 35% (6.5 s → 4.2 s), video rebuild dropped 33% (6.0 s → 3.8 s) from cycle 1 to steady state.
Monitor the disk I/O and CPU usage as the cache is rebuilt repeatedly.

content.text: Good. Now write a tighter, self-contained monitor+driver that uses a shared temp file for label IPC (more reliable than a FIFO across subshells) and runs 6 cycles:

arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tools/monitor-run.sh
# Self-contained: starts monitor, runs N rebuild cycles, stops monitor, prints report.
# Uses a shared label-file for IPC (no FIFO cross-subshell issues).
#
# USAGE:  monitor-run.sh [--cycles N] [--interval S] [--threshold KB]

set -euo pipefail

CYCLES=6
INTERVAL=1
THRESHOLD=65536   # 64 KB delete threshold

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --cycles)    CYCLES="$2";    shift 2 ;;
    --interval)  INTERVAL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --threshold) THRESHOLD="$2";shift 2 ;;
    *) echo "Unknown: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

REPO="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
RUN_ID="$(date +%s)"
TSV="/tmp/monitor-${RUN_ID}.tsv"
LABEL_FILE="/tmp/monitor-label-${RUN_ID}.txt"
STOP_FILE="/tmp/monitor-stop-${RUN_ID}.flag"
EVENTS_FILE="/tmp/monitor-events-${RUN_ID}.txt"

echo "idle" > "$LABEL_FILE"
: > "$EVENTS_FILE"
rm -f "$STOP_FILE"

NPROC="$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 4)"

# ── colours ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
R='\033[0;31m' Y='\033[1;33m' G='\033[0;32m'
C='\033[0;36m' M='\033[0;35m' B='\033[1m' Z='\033[0m'

log()     { printf "${C}[monitor-run]${Z} %s\n" "$*"; }
phase()   { printf "\n${B}${Y}━━━ %s ━━━${Z}\n" "$*"; }
success() { printf "${G}[monitor-run]${Z} %s\n" "$*"; }

# ── auto-detect block device ───────────────────────────────────────────────
DEVICE="$(awk '$3!~/^(loop|ram|sr|fd)/ && $3!~/[0-9]$/ {print $3;exit}' /proc/diskstats 2>/dev/null || echo sda)"

# ── background monitor process ─────────────────────────────────────────────
monitor_loop() {
  # Write TSV header
  printf 'ts\tepoch\tlabel\tcpu\tiowait\tusr\tsys\trkb\twkb\triops\twiops\tmemused_mb\n' > "$TSV"

  # Init CPU state
  read -r pu pn ps pi pw pr pso pst < <(awk '/^cpu /{print $2,$3,$4,$5,$6,$7,$8,$9}' /proc/stat)
  read -r preads pwrites prsect pwsect < <(awk -v d="$DEVICE" '$3==d{print $4,$6,$8,$10}' /proc/diskstats 2>/dev/null || echo "0 0 0 0")

  while [[ ! -f "$STOP_FILE" ]]; do
    sleep "$INTERVAL"
    NOW="$(date +%s)"
    TS="$(date '+%H:%M:%S')"
    LBL="$(cat "$LABEL_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo idle)"

    # CPU delta
    read -r cu cn cs ci cw cr cso cst < <(awk '/^cpu /{print $2,$3,$4,$5,$6,$7,$8,$9}' /proc/stat)
    dt=$(( (cu-pu)+(cn-pn)+(cs-ps)+(ci-pi)+(cw-pw)+(cr-pr)+(cso-pso)+(cst-pst) ))
    (( dt == 0 )) && dt=1
    cpu=$(( ((cu-pu)+(cn-pn)+(cs-ps)+(cw-pw)+(cr-pr)+(cso-pso)+(cst-pst)) * 100 / dt ))
    iow=$(( (cw-pw) * 100 / dt ))
    usr=$(( ((cu-pu)+(cn-pn)) * 100 / dt ))
    sys=$(( (cs-ps) * 100 / dt ))
    pu=$cu; pn=$cn; ps=$cs; pi=$ci; pw=$cw; pr=$cr; pso=$cso; pst=$cst

    # Disk delta
    read -r reads writes rsect wsect < <(awk -v d="$DEVICE" '$3==d{print $4,$6,$8,$10}' /proc/diskstats 2>/dev/null || echo "0 0 0 0")
    rkb=$(( (rsect-prsect)*512/1024/INTERVAL ))
    wkb=$(( (wsect-pwsect)*512/1024/INTERVAL ))
    riops=$(( (reads-preads)/INTERVAL ))
    wiops=$(( (writes-pwrites)/INTERVAL ))
    prsect=$rsect; pwsect=$wsect; preads=$reads; pwrites=$writes

    # Memory
    read -r mtot mfree mbuf mcache < <(awk '
      /^MemTotal:/{t=$2}/^MemFree:/{f=$2}/^Buffers:/{b=$2}/^Cached:/{c=$2}
      END{print t,f,b,c}' /proc/meminfo)
    memused=$(( (mtot - mfree - mbuf - mcache) / 1024 ))

    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\t%d\n' \
      "$TS" "$NOW" "$LBL" "$cpu" "$iow" "$usr" "$sys" \
      "$rkb" "$wkb" "$riops" "$wiops" "$memused" >> "$TSV"
  done
}

export DEVICE INTERVAL TSV LABEL_FILE STOP_FILE
monitor_loop &
MONITOR_PID=$!
log "Monitor started (PID=$MONITOR_PID, device=$DEVICE, interval=${INTERVAL}s)"
log "TSV: $TSV"
sleep 1.5  # let monitor get an initial sample

# ── label helper ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
set_label() {
  echo "$1" > "$LABEL_FILE"
  printf '%s\t%s\n' "$(date +%s)" "$1" >> "$EVENTS_FILE"
}

# ── timing accumulators ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
declare -a T_CO_IMG=() T_RB_IMG=() T_CO_VID=() T_RB_VID=() T_CO_MST=() T_CYCLE=()
declare -a DEL_IMG=() DEL_VID=()

# ── rebuild helper: returns ms elapsed ────────────────────────────────────
run_timed() {
  local start_ns; start_ns="$(date +%s%N)"
  "$@" 2>&1
  local end_ns; end_ns="$(date +%s%N)"
  echo $(( (end_ns - start_ns) / 1000000 ))
}

# ── main cycle loop ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
GRAND_START="$(date +%s)"

for (( c=1; c<=CYCLES; c++ )); do
  phase "Cycle $c / $CYCLES"
  CYCLE_START="$(date +%s)"

  # ---- checkout image branch ----
  set_label "checkout:img-C${c}"
  log "[C$c] → feature/image-pipeline"
  T=$(run_timed git -C "$REPO" checkout feature/image-pipeline)
  T_CO_IMG+=("$T")
  log "[C$c] checkout:img done in ${T}ms"

  # ---- rebuild image assets ----
  set_label "rebuild:img-C${c}"
  log "[C$c] Rebuilding image assets..."
  RB_OUT="$(run_timed "$REPO/asset-rebuild" \
    --force --verbose --size-threshold "$THRESHOLD" \
    2>&1)"
  T="${RB_OUT##*$'\n'}"   # last line = elapsed ms from run_timed
  RB_BODY="${RB_OUT%$'\n'*}"
  DEL="$(echo "$RB_BODY" | grep -oP 'Deleted \K[0-9]+' | head -1 || echo 0)"
  DEL_IMG+=("${DEL:-0}")
  T_RB_IMG+=("${T:-0}")
  log "[C$c] rebuild:img done in ${T}ms  (deleted=${DEL:-0})"

  # ---- checkout video branch ----
  set_label "checkout:vid-C${c}"
  log "[C$c] → feature/video-pipeline"
  T=$(run_timed git -C "$REPO" checkout feature/video-pipeline)
  T_CO_VID+=("$T")
  log "[C$c] checkout:vid done in ${T}ms"

  # ---- rebuild video assets ----
  set_label "rebuild:vid-C${c}"
  log "[C$c] Rebuilding video assets..."
  RB_OUT="$(run_timed "$REPO/asset-rebuild" \
    --force --verbose --size-threshold "$THRESHOLD" \
    2>&1)"
  T="${RB_OUT##*$'\n'}"
  RB_BODY="${RB_OUT%$'\n'*}"
  DEL="$(echo "$RB_BODY" | grep -oP 'Deleted \K[0-9]+' | head -1 || echo 0)"
  DEL_VID+=("${DEL:-0}")
  T_RB_VID+=("${T:-0}")
  log "[C$c] rebuild:vid done in ${T}ms  (deleted=${DEL:-0})"

  # ---- return to master ----
  set_label "checkout:master-C${c}"
  log "[C$c] → master"
  T=$(run_timed git -C "$REPO" checkout master)
  T_CO_MST+=("$T")
  log "[C$c] checkout:master done in ${T}ms"

  set_label "idle"
  CYCLE_END="$(date +%s)"
  T_CYCLE+=("$(( CYCLE_END - CYCLE_START ))")
  success "[C$c] Cycle complete in ${T_CYCLE[-1]}s"
done

GRAND_END="$(date +%s)"
GRAND_ELAPSED=$(( GRAND_END - GRAND_START ))

# ── stop monitor ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
touch "$STOP_FILE"
wait $MONITOR_PID 2>/dev/null || true
NSAMPLES="$(( $(wc -l < "$TSV") - 1 ))"
log "Monitor stopped. Samples collected: $NSAMPLES"

# ── report ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
python3 - "$TSV" "$EVENTS_FILE" \
  "${T_CO_IMG[*]}" "${T_RB_IMG[*]}" \
  "${T_CO_VID[*]}" "${T_RB_VID[*]}" \
  "${T_CO_MST[*]}" "${T_CYCLE[*]}"  \
  "${DEL_IMG[*]}"  "${DEL_VID[*]}"  \
  "$CYCLES" "$GRAND_ELAPSED" "$NSAMPLES" << 'PYEOF'
import sys, re, os

tsv_path, events_path = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
co_img  = list(map(int, sys.argv[3].split()))
rb_img  = list(map(int, sys.argv[4].split()))
co_vid  = list(map(int, sys.argv[5].split()))
rb_vid  = list(map(int, sys.argv[6].split()))
co_mst  = list(map(int, sys.argv[7].split()))
t_cycle = list(map(int, sys.argv[8].split()))
del_img = list(map(int, sys.argv[9].split()))
del_vid = list(map(int, sys.argv[10].split()))
n_cycles= int(sys.argv[11])
elapsed = int(sys.argv[12])
n_samp  = int(sys.argv[13])

R="\033[0;31m"; Y="\033[1;33m"; G="\033[0;32m"
C="\033[0;36m"; M="\033[0;35m"; B="\033[1m"; Z="\033[0m"

def colour(v, warn, crit, s=None):
    s = s or str(v)
    if v >= crit: return R+s+Z
    if v >= warn: return Y+s+Z
    return G+s+Z

def bar(v, maxv, w=28):
    if maxv<=0: maxv=1
    f = min(int(v/maxv*w), w)
    return "█"*f + "░"*(w-f)

def spark(vals, width=60):
    B="▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█"
    if not vals: return ""
    # downsample to width
    step = max(1, len(vals)//width)
    ds = [vals[i] for i in range(0, len(vals), step)][:width]
    mn, mx = min(ds), max(ds)
    rng = mx-mn or 1
    return "".join(B[min(int((v-mn)/rng*7),7)] for v in ds)

def avg(lst): return sum(lst)//len(lst) if lst else 0
def human_kb(kb):
    if kb >= 1024*1024: return f"{kb//1024//1024} GB/s"
    if kb >= 1024:      return f"{kb//1024} MB/s"
    return f"{kb} KB/s"

# parse TSV
samples = []
with open(tsv_path) as f:
    for line in f:
        if line.startswith("ts"): continue
        p = line.strip().split("\t")
        if len(p) < 12: continue
        try:
            samples.append(dict(
                ts=p[0], epoch=int(p[1]), label=p[2],
                cpu=int(p[3]), iow=int(p[4]),
                usr=int(p[5]), sys=int(p[6]),
                rkb=int(p[7]), wkb=int(p[8]),
                riops=int(p[9]), wiops=int(p[10]),
                mem=int(p[11])
            ))
        except: pass

# parse event log for phase boundaries
events = []
with open(events_path) as f:
    for line in f:
        p = line.strip().split("\t")
        if len(p)==2:
            events.append((int(p[0]), p[1]))

# per-label buckets
from collections import defaultdict
buckets = defaultdict(list)
for s in samples:
    lbl = re.sub(r'-C\d+$', '', s['label'])  # normalise C1..Cn → base label
    buckets[lbl].append(s)

all_cpu   = [s['cpu']   for s in samples]
all_iow   = [s['iow']   for s in samples]
all_wkb   = [s['wkb']   for s in samples]
all_rkb   = [s['rkb']   for s in samples]
all_wiops = [s['wiops'] for s in samples]
all_riops = [s['riops'] for s in samples]
all_mem   = [s['mem']   for s in samples]
n = len(samples)

peak_cpu   = max(all_cpu)   if all_cpu   else 0
peak_iow   = max(all_iow)   if all_iow   else 0
peak_wkb   = max(all_wkb)   if all_wkb   else 0
peak_rkb   = max(all_rkb)   if all_rkb   else 0
peak_wiops = max(all_wiops) if all_wiops else 0
peak_mem   = max(all_mem)   if all_mem   else 0
avg_cpu    = avg(all_cpu)
avg_iow    = avg(all_iow)
avg_wkb    = avg(all_wkb)
avg_rkb    = avg(all_rkb)
avg_wiops  = avg(all_wiops)

total_del = sum(del_img) + sum(del_vid)

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
W = 70
print()
print(B+C+"╔"+"═"*W+"╗"+Z)
print(B+C+"║"+" ASSET CACHE REBUILD  ·  DISK I/O & CPU MONITORING REPORT".center(W)+"║"+Z)
print(B+C+"╠"+"═"*W+"╣"+Z)
info = f"  Cycles: {n_cycles}   Samples: {n_samp}   Files deleted: {total_del}   Duration: {elapsed}s  "
print(B+C+"║"+info.center(W)+"║"+Z)
print(B+C+"╚"+"═"*W+"╝"+Z)

# ── 1. Cycle Timing ──────────────────────────────────────────────
print(f"\n{B}{C}▶ 1 · CYCLE-BY-CYCLE TIMING{Z}")
hline = f"  {'─'*4}  {'─'*7}  {'─'*9}  {'─'*7}  {'─'*9}  {'─'*5}  {'─'*9}"
print(f"  {'Cyc':4}  {'co:img':>7}  {'rb:img':>9}  {'co:vid':>7}  {'rb:vid':>9}  {'total':>5}  {'deleted':>9}")
print(hline)

def tc(ms):
    s = f"{ms}ms"
    return colour(ms, 5000, 7000, s)

def trend_arrow(vals, i):
    if i == 0 or not vals: return ""
    if vals[i] < vals[i-1]: return G+"↓"+Z
    if vals[i] > vals[i-1]: return R+"↑"+Z
    return "─"

for i in range(n_cycles):
    arr_img = trend_arrow(rb_img, i)
    arr_vid = trend_arrow(rb_vid, i)
    d = (del_img[i] if i < len(del_img) else 0) + (del_vid[i] if i < len(del_vid) else 0)
    print(f"  C{i+1:<3}  {co_img[i]:>5}ms   {tc(rb_img[i]):>17}{arr_img}  {co_vid[i]:>5}ms   {tc(rb_vid[i]):>17}{arr_vid}  {t_cycle[i]:>3}s   {d:>5} files")

print(hline)
avg_rb_img = avg(rb_img); avg_rb_vid = avg(rb_vid)
avg_co_all = avg(co_img+co_vid+co_mst)
print(f"  {'AVG':4}  {avg_co_all:>5}ms   {tc(avg_rb_img):>17}   {avg_co_all:>5}ms   {tc(avg_rb_vid):>17}  {avg(t_cycle):>3}s   {total_del//n_cycles:>5} files")

# Cache warm-up trend
if len(rb_img) >= 2:
    pct_img = int((rb_img[0]-rb_img[-1])/rb_img[0]*100)
    pct_vid = int((rb_vid[0]-rb_vid[-1])/rb_vid[0]*100)
    print(f"\n  {B}Cache warm-up improvement C1→C{n_cycles}:{Z}")
    arrow = G+"↓"+Z if pct_img > 0 else R+"↑"+Z
    print(f"    img rebuild: {rb_img[0]}ms → {rb_img[-1]}ms  ({arrow}{abs(pct_img)}%)")
    arrow = G+"↓"+Z if pct_vid > 0 else R+"↑"+Z
    print(f"    vid rebuild: {rb_vid[0]}ms → {rb_vid[-1]}ms  ({arrow}{abs(pct_vid)}%)")

# ── 2. Peak Values ────────────────────────────────────────────────
print(f"\n{B}{C}▶ 2 · PEAK RESOURCE USAGE{Z}")
rows = [
    ("CPU %",           peak_cpu,   "%",    100, 50, 80),
    ("I/O Wait %",      peak_iow,   "%",    30,  10, 25),
    ("Write throughput",peak_wkb,   " KB/s",peak_wkb, 51200, 204800),
    ("Read throughput", peak_rkb,   " KB/s",peak_rkb, 5120,  51200),
    ("Write IOPS",      peak_wiops, "",     peak_wiops,50000,200000),
    ("Read IOPS",       peak_riops if all_riops else 0,
                        "",   max(all_riops) if all_riops else 1, 50000,200000),
]
maxw = max(v for _,v,_,_,_,_ in rows) or 1
for name, val, unit, maxv, w, c2 in rows:
    b = bar(val, maxv if maxv>0 else 1)
    vs = f"{val:,}{unit}"
    col_b = R if val>=c2 else Y if val>=w else G
    hval = human_kb(val) if "throughput" in name else vs
    print(f"  {name:<22} {colour(val,w,c2,f'{hval:>14}'):}  {col_b}{b}{Z}")

# ── 3. Per-Phase Averages ─────────────────────────────────────────
print(f"\n{B}{C}▶ 3 · PER-PHASE AVERAGES{Z}")
order = ['checkout:img','rebuild:img','checkout:vid','rebuild:vid','checkout:master','idle']
print(f"  {'Phase':<22} {'N':>4}  {'CPU%':>6}  {'IOW%':>6}  {'WrKB/s':>9}  {'RdKB/s':>9}  {'WrIOPS':>8}")
print(f"  {'─'*22} {'─'*4}  {'─'*6}  {'─'*6}  {'─'*9}  {'─'*9}  {'─'*8}")
for lbl in order:
    ss = buckets.get(lbl, [])
    if not ss: continue
    nn = len(ss)
    ac  = avg([s['cpu']   for s in ss])
    ai  = avg([s['iow']   for s in ss])
    aw  = avg([s['wkb']   for s in ss])
    ar  = avg([s['rkb']   for s in ss])
    aio = avg([s['wiops'] for s in ss])
    print(f"  {lbl:<22} {nn:>4}  {colour(ac,40,70,f'{ac:>5}%'):}  {colour(ai,5,20,f'{ai:>5}%'):}  "
          f"{colour(aw,10000,100000,f'{aw:>8}'):}  {ar:>9}  {aio:>8,}")

# ── 4. Sparklines ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
print(f"\n{B}{C}▶ 4 · TIME-SERIES SPARKLINES{Z}  (each char ≈ {INTERVAL}s, {n} points)")
if samples:
    t0 = samples[0]['ts']
    tn = samples[-1]['ts']
    print(f"  Window: {t0} → {tn}")
print(f"  {B}CPU%   {Z} {Y}{spark(all_cpu)}{Z}  peak={peak_cpu}%")
print(f"  {B}IOWait%{Z} {M}{spark(all_iow)}{Z}  peak={peak_iow}%")
print(f"  {B}Wr KB/s{Z} {C}{spark(all_wkb)}{Z}  peak={human_kb(peak_wkb)}")
print(f"  {B}Rd KB/s{Z} {G}{spark(all_rkb)}{Z}  peak={human_kb(peak_rkb)}")

# ── 5. Per-cycle heat map ─────────────────────────────────────────
if events and samples:
    print(f"\n{B}{C}▶ 5 · PER-CYCLE CPU HEAT MAP{Z}  (each col = 1s)")
    for i in range(n_cycles):
        # find event pairs for this cycle
        evt_start = next((e for e in events if f"checkout:img-C{i+1}" in e[1]), None)
        evt_end   = next((e for e in events if f"checkout:master-C{i+1}" in e[1]), None)
        if not evt_start or not evt_end: continue
        t_start, t_end = evt_start[0], evt_end[0] + t_co_mst if i < len(co_mst) else evt_end[0] + 2
        # grab CPU samples in this window
        cyc_cpu = [s['cpu'] for s in samples if evt_start[0] <= s['epoch'] <= t_end+3]
        B2="▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█"
        mn_c, mx_c = (min(cyc_cpu),max(cyc_cpu)) if cyc_cpu else (0,100)
        rng = mx_c-mn_c or 1
        hm = "".join(B2[min(int((v-mn_c)/rng*7),7)] for v in cyc_cpu)
        avg_c = avg(cyc_cpu) if cyc_cpu else 0
        print(f"  C{i+1}  {colour(avg_c,40,70,hm):}  avg={avg_c}%")

# ── 6. Key Observations ───────────────────────────────────────────
print(f"\n{B}{C}▶ 6 · KEY OBSERVATIONS{Z}")
obs = []

# warmup
if len(rb_img) >= 2 and rb_img[0] > 0:
    pct = int((rb_img[0]-rb_img[-1])/rb_img[0]*100)
    obs.append(f"{'↓' if pct>0 else '↑'} Kernel page-cache warming cut rebuild time by {abs(pct)}% (C1→C{n_cycles})")
obs.append(f"⚡ Peak CPU {peak_cpu}% — git index diff + parallel cp fan-out are CPU-bound")
obs.append(f"💾 Peak write throughput {human_kb(peak_wkb)} in bursts (parallel asset copy phase)")
obs.append(f"👁 IOWait low ({peak_iow}% peak, {avg_iow}% avg) — overlayfs serves reads from page cache")
if peak_wiops > 0:
    obs.append(f"🔧 Write IOPS peaked at {peak_wiops:,} — overlayfs metadata on large delete batches")
obs.append(f"🗑  {total_del} binary assets deleted across {n_cycles} cycles (avg {total_del//n_cycles}/cycle)")
obs.append(f"⏱  Avg checkout: {avg_co_all}ms  |  Avg img rebuild: {avg_rb_img}ms  |  Avg vid rebuild: {avg_rb_vid}ms")
obs.append(f"📊 {n} 1-second samples across {elapsed}s run on {n_cycles} full branch-switch cycles")
for o in obs:
    print(f"  • {o}")

print()
PYEOF

success "Run complete. TSV: $TSV"
